create_modal.ownership_warning_body: The created directory and compose file will be owned by the user running this action — either your regular user (limited mode) or root (superuser mode). Containers started later may run with a different UID and encounter permission errors on bind-mounted paths. This is expected behavior: some images work fine, others require specific ownership. Adjust user:, volume permissions, or run mode as needed for your stack.

scale_modal.title: Scale services — {{name}}
scale_modal.sideeffects_body: Each service replica is a separate container sharing the same image and config. Scaling up starts new containers immediately. Scaling down stops and removes the excess ones. Changes to host port bindings, volume mounts, or network aliases may cause conflicts.
scale_modal.what_is_scale_body: This runs "docker compose up -d --scale <service>=<n>". Docker Compose will start or stop containers to reach the requested count. Existing containers are not recreated unless the image or config changed.
scale_modal.port_conflict_inline: This service has static host port bindings — scaling beyond 1 replica will fail because only one container can bind a host port at a time.
scale_modal.port_conflict_body: The following services have static host port bindings. Docker will not be able to start more than one replica because a host port can only be bound by a single container:
